title: Rav Rechumi (III)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman places him among the Savoraim and finds him still mentioned in the Gemara. These are Rav Sherira Gaon’s words in the [Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon](https://www.sefaria.org/Epistle_of_Rav_Sherira_Gaon.2.16), part 2, chapter 4 in Hyman’s edition: “And after this (after the later Ravina) there were the Savoraim — such as Rav Richumi, Rav Yosef and Rav Achai of Bei Chatim”; in the Epistle printed in Seder HaChakhamim it cites “such as Rav Richumi (some versions: Nichumi), Rabbah, Rav Yosef and Rav Achai of Bei Chatim.” This lights the way for us in what they said in [Eruvin 11a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.11a.12): “What are pitchei shima’i? Rav Rechumi and Rav Yosef disagree about it”; Hyman considers both undoubtedly Savoraim, for one cannot err and say that it is Rav Rechumi, Abaye’s student, for then how would he disagree with Rav Yosef and be mentioned before him?
Hyman considers Abba Yose in Menachot 33a (compare [Menachot 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.33b.8)) an erroneous reading.

In [Eruvin 71b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.71b.12): “Rav Nichumi (Rechumi — the Rosh and Dikdukei Soferim) and Rabbah disagree about it,” and Hyman regards both as Savoraim; they had a doubt whether he was called Rechumi or Nichumi. Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim cites the reading “Rav Rechumi and Abba Yose.” Hyman dates this Rav Rechumi’s death to Nisan, year 817 (תתיז; era unspecified here). From this he concludes that the first Rav Rechumi died in Rava’s lifetime; the second died ninety-odd years after Rava, for Rava died in year 663 (תרסג) and he died in year 757 (תשנז); and the third died sixty years after the second. Hyman criticizes [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3227&lang=en) for confusing them all together and for not noticing that there were three.[^1]

notes.text: The consulted Epistle gives Rav Nichumi and reads Rabbah Yose together in its list, alongside the lists Hyman quotes. Menachot 33b gives Rav Richumi and Abba Yose for the doorway dispute, where Eruvin 11a gives Rav Rechumi and Rav Yosef. The consulted Eruvin 71b has Rabbi Nechumi and Rabbah. Heilprin brings notices together that Hyman assigns to different generations.
